name: voidbase
goal: A PocketBase-wire-compatible server on Cloudflare Workers via Void. Finish line: the unmodified PocketBase admin panel and the unmodified pocketbase JS SDK both work against it, and it is production ready.

targets.runtime: Cloudflare Workers via Void 0.10.x: D1, R2, Durable Objects, cron triggers

decisions.title: Native TypeScript port, not PocketBase-in-wasm
decisions.choice: Reimplement the wire protocol on Workers primitives.
decisions.why: PocketBase compiles to wasm unmodified (51 MB, fits), but it pins compute and storage in one Durable Object, and Void exposes no custom Durable Objects. That is a lift, not a port.

decisions.title: D1 per instance for data
decisions.choice: One D1 database per voidbase instance, raw binding for user collections, Drizzle only for system tables.
decisions.why: Read replication through the Sessions API, managed migrations, and Cloudflare's own guidance to scale out with many small databases. Accepted constraints: batch-only writes, 100 bound parameters, 100 columns per table.

decisions.title: Validate, then one batch
decisions.choice: Every write path validates with reads first, then commits a single D1 batch. Hooks run before or after the batch, never inside a transaction.
decisions.why: D1 has no interactive transactions. This is the documented semantic difference from PocketBase.

decisions.title: Queues for side effects
decisions.choice: Email, audit log rows, cascade file deletes, thumbnails, and webhook actions run in queue consumers.
decisions.why: Keeps request latency flat and matches the platform's intended use of Queues.

decisions.title: Realtime on void/sse over a D1 change feed
decisions.choice: PocketBase framing is written by void/sse. Fanout is a _changes table in D1 appended inside the write batch and polled about once a second by each open stream from inside its own request (Workers tie timers and stream writers to the request that created them); streams in one isolate share the last read. void/live stays an opt-in low-latency transport behind the same front. No sidecar, no custom Durable Object.
decisions.why: void/live holds one Durable Object per connection, billed for wall-clock duration at about $4 per always-connected client per month. The change feed costs about $0.02 per client per month and $0 when nobody is connected, and it keeps the self-host deploy path open. Revised the same day after pricing the first version.

decisions.title: Two unmodified oracles
decisions.choice: The PocketBase 0.40.2 admin panel and the pocketbase JS SDK 0.28, both untouched, define done. Schema is data, edited at runtime.
decisions.why: The panel exercises the superuser surface that apps never touch; the starter exercises the app surface.

oracles.label: SDK seamless
oracles.description: Every service method in the pocketbase JS SDK 0.28 typings behaves as it does against PocketBase 0.40.2.

oracles.label: Admin panel green
oracles.description: The unmodified PocketBase admin panel served at /_/ works screen by screen.

oracles.label: Starter app green
oracles.description: pocketbase-sveltekit-starter runs unchanged, including its JS hooks and migrations.

oracles.label: Production ready
oracles.description: Hardening, operations, docs, tests, and deploy paths a paying user needs.

areas.title: Realtime
areas.summary: PocketBase's SSE protocol emitted by void/sse, fanned out through a D1 change feed. Zero cost when nobody is connected. void/live is an opt-in low-latency transport.

items.title: GET /api/realtime as a void/sse eventStream: PB_CONNECT with the clientId as the SSE id, keepalive comments, close on client abort
items.verify: SDK realtime.isConnected becomes true against voidbase

items.title: _changes table (id, collection, recordId, action, created) appended inside the same D1 batch as the record write, so the feed is atomic with the change
POST /api/realtime stores the stream's subscriptions and auth token in _realtime_clients keyed by clientId, because the POST can land on any isolate; the stream picks them up on its next poll

Per-connection poll loop inside its own request (Workers bind timers and stream writers to the request that made them); loops in one isolate share the last change-feed read so D1 sees about one query per second per isolate; cursor per stream
items.surface: module-level poller, SELECT … FROM _changes WHERE id > ?
items.notes: Rewritten after the first shared setInterval died with the connection that created it. Verified by test/conformance/realtime.ts and the starter list updating live.

items.title: Each matched change is hydrated from D1: rule check with the subscriber's auth (listRule for coll/*, viewRule for coll/id), expand from the subscription options, record enrichment
items.surface: one D1 read per event per subscriber
items.verify: Starter posts list updates live in a second tab; a non-owner never receives a private record

items.title: Reconnect: fresh clientId on PB_CONNECT, SDK resubmits subscriptions; the client row and cursor are dropped when the stream closes
_changes and _realtime_clients retention cron; poll interval knob; documented default latency of one to two seconds
items.notes: __vbChangesCleanup__ cron every 10 minutes: _changes older than 10 minutes and _realtime_clients rows idle for 6 hours are removed.

items.title: Opt-in low-latency transport on void/live behind the same PocketBase-framed front: in-isolate bridge with live.connect as owner client:<id>, control translation, topic sharding past 256 subscribers
items.notes: Costs about $4 per always-connected client per month in Durable Object duration. Only for apps that need sub-second delivery.

areas.title: Logs
areas.summary: Request logs in D1 with the panel's list, detail, and hourly stats.

items.title: Request and activity logger writing _logs in batches after the response
items.notes: requestLogger middleware writes a _logs row after every API response through waitUntil (PocketBase's data keys: type, execTime, url, method, status, referer, userAgent, auth, authId, userIP, remoteIP, error and details on failures), honouring logs.maxDays, minLevel, logIP and logAuthId; appLog for application messages; the logs and realtime stream routes are skipped like SkipSuccessActivityLog.

items.title: Retention cron and minLevel filtering

areas.title: Backups
areas.summary: Archives of D1 data and files into R2, with restore. CPU-time bound on Workers.

items.title: Create an archive of D1 data plus a files manifest into R2
items.notes: src/server/backups.ts: POST /api/backups (name validation, uniqueness, lock) builds a zip (fflate) with data.json (every D1 table's columns and rows, logs included, change feed excluded) plus storage/<key> for every R2 file, stored under __backups__/ in R2; __pbAutoBackup__ from settings.backups.cron with cronMaxKeep pruning. test/conformance/backups.ts 17/17.

items.title: List and delete backups
items.notes: GET /api/backups ({key, modified, size}) and DELETE /api/backups/:key with PocketBase's messages (its raw error carries an OS path).

items.title: Upload and restore by recreating tables and files
items.notes: POST /api/backups/:key/restore rebuilds in the background: drops user tables/views, restores _collections, recreates tables from the schema, reloads every table's rows, replaces the R2 files. Only voidbase archives (data.json) restore; PocketBase's SQLite archives are refused with a clear error. Upload accepts any zip. Verified by a create/modify/restore round trip in backups.ts.

items.title: Download with a superuser file token
items.notes: GET /api/backups/:key?token= with a superuser file token (IP allowlist honoured), served as an attachment.

items.title: Auto backup cron and cronMaxKeep
items.notes: __pbAutoBackup__ registered from settings.backups.cron, @auto_pb_backup_ names, oldest beyond cronMaxKeep removed.

items.title: canBackup gating in health when the feature is unavailable
items.notes: health.data.canBackup is false while a backup or restore holds the lock in _params (apis/health.go semantics); possibleProxyHeader ignores CF-Connecting-IP because Workers set it themselves and it is already the real IP.

items.title: Cron registry with a per-minute trigger dispatching cron expressions
items.notes: crons/every-minute.ts (Cloudflare cron trigger) matches every registered expression against the minute: PocketBase's __pbDBOptimize__, __pbMFACleanup__, __pbOTPCleanup__, __pbLogsCleanup__, voidbase's __vbChangesCleanup__ (change feed and stale stream rows) and cronAdd jobs from pb_hooks, each inside a superuser hook store. Cron triggers do not fire in local dev; fired through /__void/scheduled with the dev trigger token.

items.title: System jobs: logs cleanup, OTP and MFA cleanup, auth origins cleanup, auto backup
items.notes: __pbDBOptimize__ (no-op on D1), __pbMFACleanup__, __pbOTPCleanup__, __pbLogsCleanup__, __pbAutoBackup__ and voidbase's __vbChangesCleanup__ on the minute trigger.

items.notes: cronAdd/cronRemove from hooks register jobs listed first in /api/crons ({id, expression}) and runnable through POST /api/crons/:id and the minute cron; fresh-db checks listing, order and execution side effect.

items.title: Conformance harness: identical requests against PocketBase and voidbase, responses diffed
items.notes: compare.ts (25), collections.ts (28), records.ts (88), thumbs.ts (58), cascade.ts (11), oauth2.ts (11), providers.ts (32), settings.ts (20), auth-flows.ts (22), otp-mfa.ts (22), batch.ts (9), protected-files.ts (9), logs-crons.ts (14), backups.ts (17), sql.ts (7), manage-rule.ts (5), filters-extra.ts (27), views.ts (11), hardening.ts (12), realtime.ts, fresh-db.ts (17), unit tests, panel-smoke, panel-collections, panel-records, panel-admin, starter-smoke, starter-passkeys and starter-oauth2 all green on 2026-09-06. Added: rules.ts (11), security.ts (69), test/sdk-suite.ts (44 SDK steps), test/panel-login.ts.

items.title: SDK coverage matrix executed live for every service method in the typings
items.notes: test/sdk-suite.ts runs the unmodified pocketbase SDK 0.28 (dev dependency) against both servers: every service method of the typings (health, client, authStore cookies, collections incl. import/scaffolds/providers/dry-run view/truncate, records CRUD + list helpers + files + thumbs, all auth flows incl. OTP/impersonate/external auths, realtime subscribe/unsubscribe through a fetch EventSource shim, batch, settings, logs, crons, sql, backups), 44 steps compared after normalization. Fixes it surfaced: collections list `filter`, POST /api/collections/meta/dry-run-view, number coercion like cast.ToFloat64, auth-methods `fields` picking, SQL console column types for expressions, S3 test wording.

items.title: Security review: rule bypass attempts, token handling, file access, injection through filters, rate limits
items.notes: test/conformance/security.ts (69 differential cases): filter/sort/fields injection, quoted/traversal collection names, hidden-field filtering, system collections as a user, superuser-only endpoints as user and guest, file/verification token misuse, tampered and stale tokens (password change invalidates), file path traversal, batch disabled, writes to views, guest user creation with verified=true, malformed bodies. Fixes from the review: PocketBase's per-endpoint malformed-body messages, RequireSameCollectionContextAuth 403 wording, files route collection message. Identifiers are whitelisted (\w+ and backquoted) and every value is a bound parameter.

items.title: Structured logging to Void logs, request metrics, error alerts
items.notes: Unhandled request errors, hook file failures and cron failures go through void/log logger.error with structured fields (method, path, job, hook, error) so `void project logs --level error` filters them; every API request is also a _logs row (panel Logs). Request metrics come from `void project requests`. Error alerting (email/webhook on error spikes) not built.
